turns_text: [SEG0001] person_1 (NURSE): Sean, I took the pressure before the doctor. First go, it was 178 over 96.
[SEG0002] person_2 (CAREGIVER): That's sky high. He was grand in the car, talking about the match.
[SEG0003] person_1 (NURSE): Let him sit quiet and I'll repeat it. The doctor is just finishing.
[SEG0004] person_3 (DOCTOR): Sean, Dr Brennan. You're in for a form, I think?
[SEG0005] person_4 (PATIENT): Knee.
[SEG0006] person_2 (CAREGIVER): Insurance form, for the community bus. He twisted the right knee stepping off last Thursday.
[SEG0007] person_3 (DOCTOR): Right knee, off the bus last Thursday, for the insurance. How is it today?
[SEG0008] person_4 (PATIENT): Grand.
[SEG0009] person_2 (CAREGIVER): Don't mind grand. He was limping to the car this morning, giving out about the step.
[SEG0010] person_3 (DOCTOR): Limping this morning. Is it actually sore, Sean?
[SEG0011] person_4 (PATIENT): Bit.
[SEG0012] person_3 (DOCTOR): A bit sore in the right knee since last Thursday, and worse when you walk?
[SEG0013] person_4 (PATIENT): Yeah.
[SEG0014] person_3 (DOCTOR): Any swelling you've seen?
[SEG0015] person_4 (PATIENT): No.
[SEG0016] person_3 (DOCTOR): No swelling. Does it give way or lock?
[SEG0017] person_4 (PATIENT): No.
[SEG0018] person_1 (NURSE): Sorry for hopping in. Second reading now he's settled, 162 over 88, pulse 76.
[SEG0019] person_3 (DOCTOR): Thanks. So 178 over 96 first, and 162 over 88 now. Still up, Sean.
[SEG0020] person_4 (PATIENT): White coat.
[SEG0021] person_3 (DOCTOR): White coat, you reckon.
[SEG0022] person_4 (PATIENT): Yeah.
[SEG0023] person_2 (CAREGIVER): He says white coat every single time. The chemist caught it high once as well, but he walked out before they repeated it.
[SEG0024] person_3 (DOCTOR): Is there a monitor at home?
[SEG0025] person_4 (PATIENT): Yeah.
[SEG0026] person_2 (CAREGIVER): In the press, hardly used. His father had a stroke around seventy, since we're talking hearts and that. Just occurred to me.

[SEG0027] person_3 (DOCTOR): Father had a stroke, I'll note that. I'm not calling this hypertension off two clinic readings. It could be the white coat, it could be the sore knee driving it up, or it could be proper high blood pressure. I will not decide which today.
[SEG0028] person_3 (DOCTOR): Any headache with it?
[SEG0029] person_4 (PATIENT): No.
[SEG0030] person_3 (DOCTOR): Chest pain, or shortness of breath?
[SEG0031] person_4 (PATIENT): No.
[SEG0032] person_3 (DOCTOR): Dizziness?
[SEG0033] person_4 (PATIENT): No.
[SEG0034] person_3 (DOCTOR): No headache, no chest pain, no breathlessness, no dizziness. Tablets?
[SEG0035] person_4 (PATIENT): No.
[SEG0036] person_2 (CAREGIVER): Only paracetamol when the knee nags. Two of the 500 milligram tablets.
[SEG0037] person_3 (DOCTOR): Two 500s. How often would that be?
[SEG0038] person_2 (CAREGIVER): Maybe twice in the day, and not every day. Only if he's hobbling.
[SEG0039] person_4 (PATIENT): Yeah.
[SEG0040] person_3 (DOCTOR): Paracetamol, two 500 milligram tablets, up to twice a day, not daily. Any drug allergies?
[SEG0041] person_4 (PATIENT): No.
[SEG0042] person_3 (DOCTOR): None. Right knee now. No swelling to see, it bends and straightens fully, tender on the inner side, and it doesn't give when I stress it.
[SEG0043] person_4 (PATIENT): Ow.
[SEG0044] person_3 (DOCTOR): Tender, yes, sorry. The form can say a minor sprain, and that you're fit for the bus if you mind the step.
[SEG0045] person_3 (DOCTOR): For the pressure I was going to start a tablet today, amlodipine 5 milligrams. Well, actually, tell me what the home yoke reads before I write the script.
[SEG0046] person_2 (CAREGIVER): He'll park them in a drawer, doctor. The once he used the yoke at home it was one-thirty. He said one-thirty.
[SEG0047] person_4 (PATIENT): One-thirty.

[SEG0048] person_3 (DOCTOR): One-thirty at home, and a tablet would only sit in the drawer. Right, I'll change that. No new tablet today. Morning and evening readings for a fortnight, and bring the book back to me.
[SEG0049] person_2 (CAREGIVER): I'll leave the machine on the kitchen table or he'll forget it exists.
[SEG0050] person_3 (DOCTOR): Sit five minutes first, feet down, cuff on the bare arm, not just in from the stairs. Write both numbers.
[SEG0051] person_3 (DOCTOR): Knee can have the same paracetamol, ice if it swells, and walking is fine. I'll sign the form on the way out.
[SEG0052] person_3 (DOCTOR): Reception will book the fortnight. If the home figures are over 160, don't sit on it, ring us before then.
